description: Bhagavad Gītā 14.11–14.13: when light — knowledge — arises in all the gates of this body, sattva has increased; greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness and longing arise when rajas has increased; absence of light, inactivity, heedlessness and delusion when tamas has increased.

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

description: Bhagavad Gītā 14.22–14.25: the marks and conduct of one beyond the guṇas — does not hate illumination, activity and delusion when present nor long for them when gone; sits as one indifferent, unshaken, knowing that the guṇas act; the same in pain and pleasure, abiding in himself, alike toward clod, stone and gold, the pleasant and the unpleasant, blame and self-praise, honour and dishonour, friend and foe; has given up all undertakings.

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

description: Bhagavad Gītā 13.28–13.31 (13.27–30 in the 700-verse numbering): 'who sees the supreme lord abiding equally in all beings, not perishing when they perish — that one sees'; seeing the lord equally present everywhere one does not harm oneself by oneself; whoever sees actions done by prakṛti alone and oneself as not the doer sees; when one sees the separate existence of beings resting in the one and spreading out from it alone, one reaches brahman.

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

description: Bhagavad Gītā 15.10–15.11: the deluded do not perceive the living being departing, staying or enjoying, accompanied by the guṇas; those with the eye of knowledge see it; yogins who strive see it abiding in themselves, while those who have not formed themselves, lacking thought, do not see it even though they strive.

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.
